sources.locator: "Transfer of the Portuguese court to Brazil", revision 1373720625

explanation: The court did not have to build a seat of government when it arrived, because one was standing. Rio had been the capital of the State of Brazil since 1763 and the king’s representative there had been styled Viceroy since then; from 1808 the same city held the government of the whole empire, which some historians call a metropolitan reversal. Forty-four years is a long precondition, and that is what the type says: without it the transfer would have been a different and much harder thing, but 1763 did not bring 1807 about.
